title: Chorus and stereo
learned: A chorus adds slightly detuned, swaying copies: one voice sounds like several
Stereo = a different signal for each side; a stereo effect makes two from one
A console channel is mono: a stereo sound takes two channels, panned left and right

steps.why: A single oscillator sounds narrow, right in the middle. A chorus makes copies of the sound whose pitch sways slightly, each a little differently, and puts them left and right. The result is wide, like several instruments playing together.
steps.do: Slow, long notes play into channel 1 of the console. A chorus (JX-CHR) is in the rack. Press Next.

steps.why: The chorus has a mono input (IN L alone is enough) and a stereo output.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from OUT 1 of the amplifier to IN L of the chorus.
steps.after: The chorus gets the sound, but its outputs go nowhere yet.

steps.why: A console channel is mono, so the two sides of a stereo sound take two channels.
steps.do: Drag OUT L of the chorus to IN 1 of the console (it replaces the amplifier's cable) and OUT R to IN 2.
steps.after: Richer, but still in the middle: both channels sit at the centre, so both speakers get both sides.

steps.do: Press F3. Turn PAN of channel 1 fully left and PAN of channel 2 fully right.
steps.after: Now it is wide: the left speaker plays one set of swaying copies, the right another, and the sound seems to fill the room between them. That is stereo: two different signals, not the same one twice. Press Tab to go back to the rack.

steps.why: DEPTH is how far the copies sway, RATE how fast.
steps.do: In the rack, press F1 and turn DEPTH of the chorus, then RATE.
steps.after: Little depth and a slow rate: a gentle shimmer. Much depth or a fast rate: a seasick wobble. The chorus is a short delay whose time moves; that is why the pitch of the copies sways.
steps.try: Flip MODE to ENSMBL: three voices at once, the lush string-machine sound of the 1970s.

steps.do: One voice, a stereo effect, two channels panned apart: width. Press Next to finish.
